Here’s a detailed 12-week couch-to-5K plan tailored for a 24-year-old client with exercise-induced asthma (EIA) controlled on a short-acting beta-agonist (SABA). It emphasizes a thorough warm-up, gradual progression, and careful monitoring of asthma symptoms, with options to adjust for cold air and intensity. It includes weekly structure, session-by-session workouts, progression logic, strength and mobility work, and basic nutrition/recovery guidance.

Key safety and asthma considerations
- Pre-exercise: Ensure he uses his SABA as prescribed 5–15 minutes before more intense efforts if symptoms are likely (as advised by his physician). Carry reliever inhaler during workouts.
- Warm-up protocol: Start with 10 minutes of light aerobic movement plus dynamic mobility, then a short interval at sub-threshold intensity to reduce EIA risk.
- Cold air: When training outdoors in cold weather, consider a mask/scarf over the mouth, or perform the warm-up indoors before moving outside; choose late-mafore outdoor sessions when air is warmer or opt for a treadmill if available.
- Progression: If EIA symptoms occur during a session (wheezing, chest tightness, coughing, excessive shortness of breath), stop, use rescue inhaler as needed, and switch to a lower-intensity session or rest day. If symptoms persist, consult their clinician.
- General safety: Ensure good hydration, adequate sleep, and consistent fueling. Include a 48-hour recovery plan after hard sessions and listen to the body.

Program structure overview
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Frequency: 3 running-focused sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Sat)
- Cross-training/strength: 2 days per week for general fitness and injury prevention (could be on non-running days)
- Optional rest days: 1–2 days as needed
- Output goal: Build from couch to completing a 5K (approximately 30–40 minutes depending on pacing)

Phases and week-by-week plan
Phase 1: Foundation and asthma-friendly conditioning (Weeks 1–3)
Goal: Establish consistent habit, improve base aerobic capacity, and reduce EIA risk with a thorough warm-up.

Week 1
- Session A (Walk/Run, 20–25 minutes total)
  - Warm-up: 10 minutes brisk walking, 5 minutes dynamic mobility (hips, ankles, thoracic spine), 2–3 minutes gentle jog.
  - Main: 1 minute jog, 2 minutes walk x 6 cycles (total ~18 minutes of activity; adjust as needed)
  - Cool-down: 5 minutes easy walking, 5 minutes static stretching (quads, calves, hamstrings, hip flexors)
- Session B (Strength + Mobility, 30–35 minutes)
  - Circuit (2 rounds): Bodyweight squats 12, push-ups or incline push-ups 10, glute bridges 15, bird dogs 10 per side, walking lunges 10 per leg, planks 20–30 seconds
  - Mobility: hip circles, ankle mobility, thoracic rotations
- Session C (Walk/Run, 25–30 minutes)
  - Similar structure to Session A but with 1.5 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk x 6, aim to finish with a 2–3 minute easy jog

Week 2
- Session A: 1.5 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk x 6 → total ~20 minutes active time
- Session B: Strength with light resistance (bands optional): goblet squats 12, Romanian deadlifts with light dumbbells 12, push-ups 10, single-leg Romanian deadlifts 8 per leg, side planks 20 seconds per side
- Session C: 2 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk x 6 → total ~24 minutes

Week 3
- Session A: 2 minutes jog, 1.5 minutes walk x 7 → total ~23 minutes
- Session B: Strength: add a posterior chain emphasis (hip hinges, hamstring curls with bands if available), core finisher: dead bug 10 per side
- Session C: 3 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk x 5 → total ~25 minutes

Phase 2: Gaining running tolerance with longer continuous blocks (Weeks 4–6)
Goal: Increase time running and reduce walking intervals; maintain warm-up emphasis to manage EIA.

Week 4
- Session A: Run 4 minutes, walk 2 minutes x 4 → total ~28 minutes
- Session B: Strength (full body) + mobility (2–3 sets per exercise)
- Session C: Run 5 minutes, walk 2 minutes x 4 → total ~28 minutes

Week 5
- Session A: Run 6 minutes, walk 2 minutes x 3 → total ~24 minutes
- Session B: Strength: add tempo: split squats, overhead press (if safe), rows with bands
- Session C: Run 8 minutes, walk 1 minute x 3 → total ~25 minutes

Week 6
- Session A: Run 9 minutes, walk 1 minute x 2 → total ~20 minutes
- Session B: Strength with increased reps: 2–3 sets of 12–15 for main lifts, core circuit
- Session C: Run 10 minutes, walk 1–2 minutes x 2 → total ~22 minutes

Phase 3: Build steady run duration and introduce continuous runs (Weeks 7–9)
Goal: Hit longer continuous intervals; start cementing run/walk pattern for 5K pace.

Week 7
- Session A: Continuous run 15 minutes, walk 2 minutes, run 5 minutes → total ~22–25 minutes
- Session B: Strength emphasizing hips and glutes; single-leg work; core
- Session C: Run 12 minutes continuous, 2 minutes walk, 10 minutes continuous

Week 8
- Session A: Run 18 minutes continuous, walk 2 minutes, 10 minutes continuous
- Session B: Resistance training: 3 sets of 12–15 for compound moves; mobility
- Session C: Run 20 minutes continuous, easy pace

Week 9
- Session A: Run 22 minutes continuous, easy pace
- Session B: Strength: focus on form and tempo; add light tempo intervals (30 seconds hard, 90 seconds easy) x4 within main set
- Session C: Run 12–14 minutes easy, 6 minutes brisk but conversational pace, 6 minutes easy

Phase 4: Peak endurance and 5K readiness (Weeks 10–12)
Goal: Complete a longer continuous run, simulate 5K distance, finalize pacing strategy.

Week 10
- Session A: Run 26–28 minutes continuous, easy pace
- Session B: Strength + mobility; emphasize trunk stability and hip strength
- Session C: Run 20–25 minutes continuous with one 5-minute block at moderate pace

Week 11
- Session A: Run 28–30 minutes continuous; aim for consistent pace
- Session B: Light recovery session: mobility, core, and 20–25 minutes of easy cardio
- Session C: Run 25–30 minutes continuous at a comfortable pace; finish with 5 minutes at a slightly faster but controlled pace

Week 12
- Session A: Practice 5K readiness: 30–32 minutes continuous at a comfortable pace + 10-minute warm-up and 5-minute cooldown
- Session B: Taper and mobility; light strength work
- Session C: Optional easy run or walk, 20–25 minutes; focus on recovery and race-day prep

Pace and progression cues
- Run/walk ratios: Start with longer walking segments and gradually increase running duration as Week 4–6 progress; aim for a steady progression with the least drop in form.
- Perceived exertion: Keep running segments at a level where conversation is possible but challenging (roughly RPE 4–6 on a 10-point scale during the running portions).
- Finishing five weeks: By Week 9–12, aim for 30 minutes of continuous running, or a 5K time close to your pace target, while maintaining form and breathing control.

Strength and mobility components
- Frequency: 2 days per week
- Core work: planks (30–45 seconds), side planks (20–30 seconds per side), dead bugs (10 per side)
- Hip/ankle strength: split squats, glute bridges, clamshells, minimal-to-mod resistance band exercises
- Mobility: daily 5–10 minutes focusing on hips, calves, ankles, thoracic spine
- Injury prevention: include proximal hamstring strengthening (glute bridges with a hamstring emphasis), rotator cuff stability if needed for upper body balance, and foam rolling as needed

Asthma management notes for training
- Warm-up routine: Always start with 10 minutes gentle cardio (walking or cycling) plus dynamic mobility. This reduces EIA risk before the interval work.
- Cold air management: If training outdoors in cold air, consider indoor onset or use a breathable mask/scarf to warm air. Warm-up indoors first; consider scheduling outdoor sessions when temperatures are more tolerable.
- Inhaler use: If symptoms present, use SABA as prescribed and switch to a lower-intensity session or rest. If symptoms persist beyond 15–20 minutes, seek medical advice.
- Monitoring: Keep a log of symptoms, peak flow if available, and exercise tolerance. Use objective measures where possible (distance, pace, and heart rate) to guide progression.

Nutrition and recovery basics
- Hydration: At least 2–3 liters per day, more around workouts.
- Protein intake: Aim for 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day to support recovery and adaptation.
- Carbohydrate timing: Consume a balanced meal or snack 1–3 hours before workouts; post-workout, include protein and carbohydrates within 1–2 hours.
- Recovery: 7–9 hours sleep; 1–2 rest days per week; lightweight mobility or walking on easy days to promote recovery.
- Gut health and appetite: Ensure vegetables, fruit, whole grains, and lean proteins are included to support energy levels.

Progress tracking and adjustments
- Weekly check-ins: Note running time, distance, pace, and perceived effort; jot down any asthma symptoms and overall energy.
- Adjustments: If EIA is triggered frequently, incorporate more gradual progression, add extra warm-up time, or shift more sessions to RPE-based progress rather than distance. If fatigue or soreness accumulates, include extra rest or an extra recovery day.
- Race readiness test: In Week 12, simulate a 5K by running the distance at a comfortable, sustainable pace and finish with a cooldown.

Sample weekly structure (example)
- Monday: Run-focused session (Week 1: 20–25 minutes total with run/walk intervals) + light mobility
- Tuesday: Rest or active recovery (light walk, mobility)
- Wednesday: Strength + Mobility
- Thursday: Rest or light cardio (cycling or swim)
- Friday: Run-focused session or easy run (Week 2–3 progression)
- Saturday: Optional cross-training (bike, row, or swim) + mobility
- Sunday: Rest

Notes for you as the trainer
- Personalize: If the client has any known allergies or intolerances, adjust nutrition guidance accordingly.
- Ensure safety: If asthma symptoms are not controlled or intensify, consult his clinician for a tailored plan, including potential adjustment of SABA usage before workouts.
- Communication: Encourage him to keep a simple log of workouts, symptoms, and any environmental factors (temperature, humidity, pollution) to refine the plan.

Here is a complete, integrated 12-week couch-to-5K plan for your client with all adjustments applied: asthma/EIA safety, warm-ups, strength work (2 days/week), intervals, tempo days, a Parkrun-style test option in Week 8, a dedicated finisher/race-day prep week, and the pacing/structure shifts you requested (pushing pace in later weeks). The plan is laid out week-by-week with session-by-session details, plus notes on nutrition, recovery, and safety. Use the Week 13 finisher week as an optional wrap-up or taper that can precede a race or Parkrun if you choose.

Assumptions and general structure
- Frequency
  - Running-focused sessions: 3 per week (Interval, Tempo, Steady/Near-threshold)
  - Strength sessions: 2 per week (S1 and S2)
  - Mobility: daily 5–10 minutes
  - Rest/recovery: 1–2 days as needed
- Equipment options: bodyweight, dumbbells, resistance bands, kettlebell; all exercises are scalable
- Progression philosophy: gradual but consistent progression with EIA safety. If symptoms flare, scale back intensity, extend warm-ups, or substitute with run-walk intervals.

Week 1
- Focus: Foundation; establish habit; baseline strength
- Session A: Run/Walk (Foundation)
  - Warm-up: 10 minutes brisk walk + 5 minutes dynamic mobility
  - Main: 1 minute jog / 2 minutes walk x 6 (approx. 18 minutes running total)
  - Cool-down: 5 minutes easy walk + 5 minutes static stretches (quads, calves, hamstrings, hip flexors)
- Session B: Strength S1 (Lower/Posterior emphasis)
  - Goblet squat or bodyweight squat: 2–3 x 10–12
  - Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells: 2–3 x 10–12
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 12
  - Bulgarian split squat: 2–3 x 8–10 per leg
  - Calf raises: 2–3 x 12–15
  - Core: dead bug or bird dog 2–3 x 10 per side
- Session C: Run/Walk (Right-size progression)
  - 1.5 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk x 6 (adjust to feel)
  - Finish with 2–3 minutes easy jog

Week 2
- Session A: Run/Walk progression
  - 1.5 minutes jog, 2 minutes walk x 6 (aim ~20 minutes active)
- Session B: Strength S2 (Anterior/Core stability and upper body)
  - Push-ups or incline push-ups: 3 x 8–12

Asthma safety and management throughout the plan
- Inhaler: carry your reliever inhaler whenever you train; consider pre-exercise inhaler if advised by clinician for higher-intensity days (intervals and tempo).
- Warm-up: always start with 8–12 minutes of light cardio plus dynamic mobility; finish with 4 strides to acclimate to running mechanics.
- Cold air: if training outdoors in cold air, use a scarf or breathable mask over mouth, or warm up indoors before stepping outside; consider treadmill options if available.
- Monitoring: maintain a symptom log, daily peak flow if available, and track RPE for all key sessions.
- If symptoms arise: stop, use inhaler, switch to run-walk or lower-intensity sessions; consult clinician if symptoms persist.

- Sleep: 7–9 hours
- Recovery: 1–2 rest days weekly; mobility daily

- Weekly check-ins: track run times, distance, pace, interval outcomes, tempo blocks, and asthma symptoms
- Adjustments: if EIA symptoms are frequent or severe, decelerate progression in tempo/interval blocks; revert to a more conservative progression until tolerance improves
